headline: Over 20,000 passengers stranded as 134 flights from Bangladesh disrupted
summary: Saudi Arabian airport restrictions due to Houthi attacks have caused widespread flight cancellations and suspensions, affecting thousands of travelers.
details: According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), 134 flights—including 61 direct and 73 transit flights—have been disrupted due to restrictions at Saudi Arabian airports.
The disruptions have affected a total of 20,254 passengers. Some flights were canceled entirely, while others were suspended.
Direct flight disruptions include 22 flights from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 from US-Bangla Airlines, 20 from Saudia Airlines, and 10 from Riyadh Air.
Transit flight disruptions involve several carriers including IndiGo (28), Emirates (H14), Emirates (14), Qatar Airways (9), FlyDubai (8), Salam Air (7), Air India (6), and Egypt Air (1).

The CAAB stated that flights to Riyadh are currently suspended due to Houthi attacks on Saudi airports. Flights to Riyadh by Biman Bangladesh Airlines are set to resume on October 25 and tomorrow, Thursday.
The situation is being monitored as airlines are attempting to manage the rescheduling of affected passengers.

headline_marked: 3 tourists [[dead, 2 missing]] after drowning at Himchari beach
headline: 3 tourists dead, 2 missing after drowning at Himchari beach
summary: Three young men from Dhaka drowned at the Himchari beach in Cox's Bazar, while two others remain missing after being swept away by large waves.
details: Three tourists from Dhaka drowned at the Himchari beach in Cox's Bazar on Wednesday afternoon. Two other members of their group remain missing after being swept away by large waves.
The victims, identified as Md. Borhan (23), Saiful Islam (23), and Nafisul Haq (22), all from Dhaka's Uttara area, were part of a 12-member group visiting the beach.
The incident occurred around 4:30 PM near the museum of the Himchari Marina Resort. Five people from the group entered the water and were quickly overwhelmed by strong waves.
Lifeguards and local residents managed to rescue three of them, but they were declared dead. Search operations for the two missing tourists continued until late evening.
Imtiaz Ahmed, regional director of the private lifeguard organization Sea-Safe, warned that many tourists are ignoring red flags in high-risk areas.
Ahmed noted that at least 20 rip currents have formed across various points of the beach, including Himchari and Laboni Point, increasing the risk of accidents.
The tragedy comes amid a massive surge in tourism, with over 300,000 visitors currently in Cox's Bazar, leaving most hotels and resorts fully booked.

3 tourists dead and 2 missing after being swept away by large waves at Himchari beach.
